title: Integrate same-leg and opposite-leg contacts into a controlled horizontal finish.
brief: The main task is one integrated hop–step–jump foot sequence from a stationary single-leg start at modest travel. Lateral entry, an elevated same-leg finish and release tasks rehearse organizing different incoming positions into forward force. This is integration, not a maximum-distance test or a claim that the full competition event has been trained.

explosive.name: Stationary Single-leg Hop–Step–Jump
explosive.job: Integrate same-leg reuse, opposite-leg transfer and a bilateral final reception into one defined horizontal foot sequence.
explosive.cue: From one foot, hop to the same foot, step-bound to the opposite foot, then jump from that foot to both feet; hold the final landing. Start the other set on the opposite leg.
explosive.regress: Shorten each segment and slow entry intent while keeping the sequence; stop for a collapsing intermediate contact or incorrect foot order.
explosive.note: Two integrated sequences = six landings: four unilateral and two bilateral. No running approach; not three bilateral broad jumps.

explosive.name: Lateral Step-in Broad Jump
explosive.job: Redirect a small lateral entry into a straight-ahead two-foot push.
explosive.cue: Take one short lateral step into a parallel two-foot gather, square the pelvis to the forward lane and jump forward; hold the landing 2 s.
explosive.regress: Shorten/slow the lateral step; stop if the jump drifts sideways or the pelvis rotates through landing.
explosive.note: Four ordinary lateral entry steps, two from each direction; each at most 1 m. This needs verified lane width.

explosive.name: Same-leg Forward Hop onto a Low Box
explosive.job: Receive one-leg forward force with full-foot placement on a raised support without assistance from the free foot.
explosive.cue: Hop from one foot to the same foot on a very low wide stable box; hold 2 s with the pelvis level, then use a controlled step-down to reset.
explosive.regress: Lower/bring the box closer; stop for partial-foot contact, free-foot rescue or pelvic collapse.
explosive.gate: Demonstrated elevated same-leg landing; no narrow or tall box.

explosive.name: Lateral-entry Forward Medicine Ball Scoop Throw
explosive.job: Square the hips after a side entry and direct leg-to-arm force forward.
explosive.cue: Take one short lateral step into a stable bilateral base, then immediately use a shallow dip and light forward scoop release with the pelvis facing the target.
explosive.regress: Slow the side step and lighten the ball; stop if the throw becomes rotational or entry balance is lost.
explosive.intent: Fast release with a light ball; retain the prescribed grounded support
explosive.note: Four ordinary side-entry steps total; no athlete flight.

explosive.name: Tall-Kneeling Forward Overhead Medicine Ball Throw
explosive.job: Express a forward long-lever arm impulse while holding the hip/trunk base steady.
explosive.cue: Kneel tall with a very light ball above the forehead; release straight forward through a quick two-arm overhead throw with knees grounded and ribs down.
explosive.regress: Use a lighter ball and smaller arm excursion; stop for back arching or uncomfortable kneeling.
explosive.intent: Fast release with a light ball; retain the prescribed grounded support

explosive.name: Forward Medicine Ball Jump Throw
explosive.job: Coordinate full-body takeoff with an airborne forward release and then recover the feet for landing.
explosive.cue: With a very light ball low in front, dip and jump modestly forward while scooping the ball forward during flight; land on both feet and hold 2 s.
explosive.regress: Use smaller flight/lighter ball; stop if the ball enters the athlete's landing zone or release disrupts foot recovery.
explosive.intent: Small crisp jump with light airborne forward release
explosive.gate: Familiar jump-release coordination and physically separated athlete/ball landing envelopes.
explosive.note: Four releases and four bilateral athlete landings are both counted; no return catch.

control.name: Standing Hip Abduction Wall Press
control.job: Lightly stabilize the support-side pelvis against lateral pressure before the next forward push.
control.cue: Stand side-on to a fixed wall/support, hold the nearer knee gently against it while the other foot supports the body; keep pelvis level and stance knee aligned.
control.regress: Use lighter pressure and a more upright stance; stop for leaning through the back or losing foot contact.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

control.name: Side-Lying Banded Clamshell
control.job: Control femoral external rotation without allowing the pelvis to roll during contact preparation.
control.cue: Lie on the side with hips/knees comfortably bent and feet together; open the top knee slightly against a light band, then lower slowly while keeping pelvis stacked.
control.regress: Use less tension/smaller opening; stop if the pelvis rolls backward or hip discomfort appears.
control.intent: Bodyweight/light resistance, easy control; at least 5 clean reps in reserve or comparable ease

strength.name: Hip Thrust — pelvic dumbbell, upper back on bench
Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs

decision: The hop–step–jump is one defined athletics foot-sequence task with all three landings counted, not a circuit of exercises hidden in one slot. Only two modest sequences are prescribed. Its single-leg start is a declared training adaptation, not a competition test. Lateral entry changes the incoming direction; the raised same-leg finish changes receiving support; the airborne ball release adds both a throw and a landing. The full sequence ends with modest strength doses rather than an assumed maximum-output peak. No before/after jump gain can be claimed because the user requested unique drills and no actual response has been supplied.
next_job: All twelve prescriptions and the full-sequence audit are complete. The next user-directed run should review actual delivery or revise a named class; do not create Class 13 or infer athlete completion.
